text: The 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive was planned around one main effort: a push south from Orikhiv to Tokmak and then Melitopol, to cut Russia's land bridge to Crimea.
The US–Ukrainian war games behind the 2023 counteroffensive imagined Ukraine reaching the Sea of Azov in 60–90 days.

observations.subject: planned time to reach the Sea of Azov

notes: Washington Post account relayed by Euromaidan Press.

text: Facing the Ukrainian main effort on the Orikhiv axis in 2023 was the Russian 58th Combined Arms Army, behind the best-prepared sector of the "Surovikin line".
RUSI describes the Surovikin line facing the Orikhiv axis as three belts about 30 km deep.
ISW had the Russian 42nd and 19th Motor Rifle Divisions heavily committed against the Orikhiv axis in June–July 2023, with Spetsnaz brigades as the counterattack force.
RUSI lists the 7th VDV and 42nd Divisions as forward on the Orikhiv axis.
On 7–8 June 2023 the Western-equipped 47th Mechanised Brigade, with Leopard 2A6s of the 33rd Mechanised Brigade, tried to breach south of Mala Tokmachka, and the first breach failed.
Mines, artillery, ATGMs and Ka-52 helicopters stopped the Ukrainian columns south of Mala Tokmachka on 7–8 June 2023.
The photographs of abandoned Leopards and Bradleys south of Mala Tokmachka in June 2023 became the emblem of the Ukrainian counteroffensive.
Within days of the failed June 2023 breach, Zaluzhnyi stopped frontal mechanized assaults.
After halting frontal mechanized assaults in June 2023, Ukraine turned to dismounted platoon and company assaults, counter-battery fire and deep strikes.
A renewed Ukrainian mechanized attack on 26 July 2023 broke into the first Russian positions east of Robotyne but did not hold its furthest gains.
Ukrainian reserves, the 82nd Air Assault and 46th Airmobile Brigades, were committed on the Orikhiv axis in mid-August 2023.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade entered Robotyne on 22 August 2023 and raised the flag there on 23 August.
Deputy Defence Minister Maliar declared Robotyne liberated on 28 August 2023.
After Robotyne, Ukrainian infantry pushed east along the Russian trench belt to Verbove in late August–September 2023.
ISW judged the Russian field fortifications west of Verbove broken on 23 September 2023.
Al Jazeera reported Ukrainian and Western sources saying the "Surovikin Line" had been cut near Verbove in September 2023.
Russia fed VDV divisions and the 41st Combined Arms Army into the Orikhiv axis in August–September 2023.
The Ukrainian salient on the Orikhiv axis stopped short of Novoprokopivka and Verbove, with no breakthrough, and by November 2023 the front was positional.
Zaluzhnyi called the war a "stalemate" in November 2023.

Maj. Gen. Ivan Popov, the 58th Army commander who had celebrated the June 2023 minefield defence, was fired on about 11–12 July 2023 after complaining about counter-battery fire and the lack of rotation.
Ukraine announced on 28 August 2023 that Robotyne was taken, after the flag was raised there on 23 August.
Ukraine held Robotyne to the end of the chapter window, 30 November 2023.
A Russian milblogger estimated on 19 September 2023 that the Ukrainian salient south of Orikhiv was at best a bulge about 7–9 km across and about 7 km deep.
Kofman and Lee put the tip of the Orikhiv salient about 10 km from the Ukrainian start line.

observations.subject: Orikhiv salient depth from the start line

text: The tip of the Ukrainian salient reached the northern edge of Novoprokopivka and the western outskirts and northern part of Verbove in September 2023, but neither village was cleared.
Tokmak, about 23 km south of Robotyne, was Tarnavskyi's "minimum goal" for the 2023 counteroffensive.
There was no Ukrainian breakthrough to Tokmak in 2023; Tokmak stayed Russian through the chapter window to 30 November 2023.
The Ukrainian MoD claimed 256.5 km² retaken by 11 September 2023 in the whole south, the Orikhiv and Velyka Novosilka axes together.
The Ukrainian MoD claimed 260 km² retaken by 18 September 2023 in the whole south, the Orikhiv and Velyka Novosilka axes together.
DeepState-derived data give a gross Ukrainian recapture of 350 km² in Q2 2023 and 294 km² in Q3 2023 for the whole front.
Forbes counted 25 Ukrainian vehicles lost in the 8 June 2023 breach south of Mala Tokmachka: 17 Bradleys, 4 Leopard 2A6, 3 Leopard 2R and 1 Wisent.
notes: OUTCOME; Forbes original paywalled, cited via Censor.NET.

text: DeepState counted irrecoverable Ukrainian losses of at least 4 APCs and 1 Leopard in the June 2023 breach south of Mala Tokmachka.
Oryx, as reported on 9 June 2023, logged 16 Bradleys and 3 Leopard 2A6 lost in the Mala Tokmachka area, of which 5 Bradleys and 1 Leopard were destroyed.
By 6 September 2023 five Leopard 2s had been destroyed in the counteroffensive, according to Forbes via the Kyiv Independent.
The first Challenger 2 lost in the war was destroyed near Robotyne by 6 September 2023.
WarSpotting has about 156 visually confirmed Russian equipment losses tagged to the Orikhiv axis for 1 June – 30 November 2023, including 41 tanks, 62 IFVs and APCs, and a Ka-52M.
Popov was dismissed as 58th Army commander on 12–13 July 2023, and his successor, Lt. Gen. Denis Lyamin, was reported removed on 9 October 2023.
notes: OUTCOME; §1 elsewhere dates the firing about 11–12 Jul.

text: On the Ukrainian side, the 47th Mechanised Brigade's commander, Oleksandr Sak, was replaced on 16 September 2023.
In October 2022 Surovikin was appointed theatre commander of Russian forces in Ukraine.
From October 2022 Russia began building deliberate defence lines in Zaporizhzhia, later called the "Surovikin line".
Western armour was pledged to Ukraine in January 2023.
Leopard 2A6s arrived in Ukraine in March 2023 and Bradleys from April 2023.
In winter–spring 2023, 47th Mechanised Brigade assault troops trained in Germany, Slovakia and Latvia.
In winter–spring 2023, 47th Mechanised Brigade Bradley crews trained for six weeks in Germany.
Eight US–Ukrainian tabletop war games shaped the 2023 counteroffensive plan in winter–spring 2023.
The Pentagon pushed for a mid-April 2023 start to the counteroffensive.
The 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive began on 4 June 2023, according to Kofman and Lee.
On 4 June 2023 milbloggers reported limited Ukrainian attacks near Mala Tokmachka.
RUSI dates the start of the Orikhiv axis attack to 3 June 2023.
On 5 June 2023 Gerasimov reportedly took command of Russian operations in the south, according to a Russian MoD claim.
The Kakhovka dam was destroyed on 6 June 2023.
On the afternoon of 7 June 2023, per DeepState, Ukraine made a first attempt south of Mala Tokmachka with two groups of 9 and 11 vehicles behind mine-clearing vehicles.
notes: group_size used for vehicle count per group.

text: In the 7 June 2023 attempt south of Mala Tokmachka, the first Ukrainian group hit mines, and the second was spotted by drones and hit by artillery.
From about 02:00 on the night of 7–8 June 2023 Ukraine made the main breach along the Mala Tokmachka–Polohy line after "extensive" artillery preparation, according to Romanchuk.
On the night of 7–8 June 2023 a first-line position of the Russian 291st and 70th Motor Rifle Regiments was penetrated, then retaken.
Before dawn on 8 June 2023 a Ukrainian assault group landed between two Russian companies near Mala Tokmachka, and Russia reported a tactical height lost at 05:00.
On 8 June 2023 Ukraine reinforced the assault near Mala Tokmachka with about 10 AFVs and about 100 troops, and the fighting lasted almost until evening.
In the opening Ukrainian assaults of June 2023 one unit missed H-hour by a couple of hours and attacked near dawn after the barrage had ended.
notes: Date unstated in the source; placed in June.

text: In the opening Ukrainian assaults of June 2023 one unit fired on friendly troops, and another was disoriented at night and stacked up.
notes: Date unstated in the source; placed in June.

text: On 8 June 2023 Russian MoD videos showed Romanchuk and Popov saying minefields played a "very important role".
On 8 June 2023 US officials called Ukrainian losses "significant".
On 8–9 June 2023 Ukrainian attacks continued south and southeast of Orikhiv, and Russia claimed the line restored.
On 8–9 June 2023 footage of damaged Western vehicles spread, and Putin acknowledged the counteroffensive had begun.
Oryx logged 2 Leopards lost (1 destroyed, 1 abandoned) as of 9 June 2023.
Russian sources said Ukraine shifted to night assaults on 10–11 June 2023.
On 10–11 June 2023 Lobkove and Piatykhatky, further west, were contested and taken by Ukraine.
About 11–12 June 2023, day 4 of the offensive, Zaluzhnyi halted frontal mechanized assaults, according to the Washington Post via Euromaidan Press.
On 12 June 2023 Maliar claimed 6.5 km and 90 km² gained in a week on the Donetsk and Tavria directions.
On 12 June 2023 the Ukrainian General Staff reported another Ka-52 downed, location unspecified.
On 13 June 2023 the Russian MoD showed a captured Leopard 2A6 and Bradleys.
Satellite imagery on 13 June 2023 showed 20 new helicopters at Berdiansk since 31 May, 27 in all, including 5 Ka-52.
On 14 June 2023 Western officials said single breach lanes were very vulnerable and that the main Russian line was up to 20 km away in places.

observations.subject: distance to the main Russian line

text: On 16 June 2023 the Ukrainian General Staff reported success towards Novodanylivka–Robotyne.
On 16 June 2023 the Russian 429th Motor Rifle Regiment (19th Division) was southwest of Orikhiv.
On 17–18 June 2023 the Wall Street Journal reported that Ukraine had "mostly paused" to re-examine tactics.
On 26 June 2023 Shershen said 1.5 km had been gained in the Melitopol direction, with demining under way.
On 7–9 July 2023 Ukraine probed towards Verbove and Kopani.
On 7–9 July 2023 a Ukrainian assault group broke in on a regimental seam northeast of Robotyne, at the 71st Regiment's 7th Company.
Early on 11 July 2023 a strike on the 58th Army's reserve command post near Berdiansk reportedly killed Lt. Gen. Oleg Tsokov, according to a milblogger.

mentions.name: Storm Shadow strike on the 58th Army reserve command post

text: On 11 July 2023 Popov's dismissal leaked.
On 11 July 2023 47th Mechanised Brigade Sergeant Major Markus asked to be demoted in protest at command decisions.
notes: Date disputed: the Kyiv Independent writes 11 June, a later Pravda note 11 September (see §11).

text: Late on 12 July 2023 Gurulyov posted Popov's voice memo on counter-battery, artillery reconnaissance and casualties, saying the army was "hit from behind by our highest boss".
Lyamin replaced Popov as commander of the 58th Combined Arms Army in July 2023.
On 18 July 2023 the Kyiv Post reported Russian barrier minefields "sometimes as much as 5 or more kilometers deep".
On 20 July 2023 Ukrainian officials reported advances of about 100 m a day south and southeast of Orikhiv.
On 20 July 2023 footage showed Ukrainian mine clearing northeast of Robotyne.
On 26 July 2023 Ukraine launched a second mechanized push towards Robotyne, which the New York Times called the "main thrust", penetrating to about 2.5 km east of Robotyne.
On 26 July 2023 Russia claimed the attack towards Robotyne involved "three battalions reinforced with tanks", and milbloggers claimed 30–80 vehicles.
Footage from 26–27 July 2023 showed two Bradleys and a T-72 abandoned about 2.5 km due east of Robotyne, and a lone vehicle at the anti-tank positions northwest of Verbove.
After 26–27 July 2023 the Ukrainian mechanized attacks east of Robotyne were not continued.
On 27 July 2023 the UK MoD reported Ka-52M helicopters with LMUR missiles (range about 15 km) in use.
On 27 July 2023 Tarnavskyi told the BBC that "most of the tasks have to be performed by troops".
On 4 August 2023 milbloggers reported Ukrainian assaults near Robotyne without armour.
On 12–13 August 2023 Ukraine reported "partial success" around Robotyne.
On 12–13 August 2023 two Ukrainian assault groups of 40–60 men took positions east of Robotyne.
On 15–16 August 2023 the 82nd Air Assault Brigade entered the fight near Robotyne: a Stryker was hit by a Lancet, and a Challenger 2 was seen.
On 15–16 August 2023 the Russian 108th VDV Regiment arrived near Robotyne.
On 16–20 August 2023 Ukrainian advances were geolocated northeast and east of Robotyne.
A milblogger said in August 2023 that Russian counter-battery problems were worst in the Zaporizhzhia direction.
On 17 August 2023 two Ka-52s were downed, one near Robotyne.
WarSpotting logged a Ka-52M lost near Novoprokopivka on 17 August 2023.
The Russian 7th VDV Division was shifted from Kherson to the Robotyne area in August 2023.
On 21–22 August 2023 the 47th Mechanised Brigade broke through to and entered Robotyne and filmed the evacuation of civilians.
On 21–22 August 2023 Russia counterattacked in the centre of Robotyne.
On 23 August 2023 the Ukrainian flag was raised in Robotyne.
On 23 August 2023 Ukraine controlled most of Robotyne and made gains west of Verbove.
On 24 August 2023 Ukrainian forces closed on the next Russian defensive belt beyond Robotyne, widening the breach.
On 25–26 August 2023 fighting reached southern Robotyne, and milbloggers complained of no rotation.
On 25–26 August 2023 elements of the Russian 76th VDV Division were shifted from Kreminna.
On 28 August 2023 Maliar announced Robotyne liberated, with advances towards Novoprokopivka and Ocheretuvate.
On 29–30 August 2023 Ukraine gained ground about 5 km southeast of Robotyne.
On 29–30 August 2023 a milblogger called the situation at Verbove "very dangerous", and Ukrainian infantry reached Verbove's northwestern outskirts.
On 31 August 2023 the Russian MoD claimed five Ukrainian assaults near Verbove repelled, and milbloggers said Ukraine was not yet through the positions just west of the village.
On 31 August – 1 September 2023 the Russian 41st Combined Arms Army began moving south, the third major Russian lateral transfer.

On 2 September 2023 Tarnavskyi told the Guardian that the first Russian line was breached, that Russia put 60% of its effort into it and 20% into each later line, and that mine clearing was possible only at night.

text: On 4–5 September 2023 counterattacks by the Russian 76th VDV were claimed to retake streets in southern Robotyne.
notes: Claimant not named in the row; Russian sources.

text: On 4–5 September 2023 Shoigu called the Zaporizhzhia direction "the tensest".
On 5–6 September 2023 the first Challenger 2 was lost near Robotyne, hit twice by artillery; the crew survived.
On 10 September 2023 Ukraine gained 1.5 km² near Robotyne, and gains east of Novoprokopivka were geolocated.
Around 10 September 2023 Leopard 2A6s fired on tree lines near Kopani and raided the Novoprokopivka tree line.
On 11 September 2023 Maliar said 256.5 km² had been retaken in the south since June.
On 11 September 2023 Milley gave "30 to 45 days" of fighting weather left for the counteroffensive.
On 16 September 2023 Sak was removed from command of the 47th Mechanised Brigade, and Col. Oleksandr Pavlii took over.
On 18 September 2023 the UK MoD said at least five VDV regiments were near Robotyne, about 10,000 men at full strength.
On 18 September 2023 Maliar claimed 260 km² retaken in the south.
On 20–21 September 2023 Ukrainian armour crossed the anti-tank ditch and dragon's teeth west of Verbove.
On 20–21 September 2023 the Wall Street Journal reported that the main Russian line near Verbove was breached.
On 22–23 September 2023 Tarnavskyi told CNN of a "breakthrough" at Verbove, with Tokmak "the minimum goal".
ISW judged on 23 September 2023 that the Russian defensive belt 1.7–3.5 km west of Verbove was broken.

observations.subject: distance of the broken belt west of Verbove

text: On 22–23 September 2023 Ukraine made its first attack into Novoprokopivka.
On 22–23 September 2023 Budanov said Romanchuk was wounded in the Black Sea Fleet HQ strike.
On 25 September 2023 Ukrainians entered northern Verbove and the fields before Novoprokopivka.
On 4 October 2023 Ukrainians held a trench along the T0408 between Robotyne and Novoprokopivka.
On 4 October 2023 the VDV claimed to push Ukrainians back 2 km near Verbove.
On 8–10 October 2023 Russia re-mined the cleared Robotyne–Verbove area.
On 8–10 October 2023 Lyamin was reportedly removed as 58th Army commander.
In October 2023, after 8–10 October, a Russian push followed near Zherebianky–Piatykhatky.
On 13–14 October 2023 Russia counterattacked along the Kopani–Robotyne–Novoprokopivka–Verbove line, claiming to push Ukrainians back.
On 17 October 2023 Ukraine made its first ATACMS strike, on the Berdiansk helicopter base.
On 24 October 2023 Ukraine made marginal gains west of Robotyne.
On 29–30 October 2023 the Kyiv Independent reported that the southern push had "run out of steam".
On 29–30 October 2023 Shoigu claimed 90,000 Ukrainian casualties in the counteroffensive; ISW called this implausible.
On 1–3 November 2023 Zaluzhnyi gave an interview and essay to The Economist calling the war a "stalemate".
On 2 November 2023 Russian sources reported Ukrainian attacks west of Robotyne and towards Myrne.
On 2 November 2023 the Russian 56th VDV Regiment was southwest of Verbove.
On 6 November 2023 Russian sources reported "positional battles" near Verbove, with periodic small Ukrainian attacks.
On 20 November 2023 Russia claimed positions near Verbove, Robotyne and Novofedorivka, which ISW did not see confirmed.
On 22 November 2023 Tarnavskyi said Russian assaults and airstrikes on the southern front were sharply up.
On 26–27 November 2023 a storm with gusts to about 46 km/h, followed by frost, hit the Robotyne area.
On 30 November 2023 Ukraine repelled 14 Russian attacks near Robotyne and Verbove, and weather impeded vehicles.
In October 2023 the 47th Mechanised Brigade, with Bradleys and Leopard 2A6s, moved to Avdiivka.
Between May 2024 and April 2025 Popov was arrested over the theft of 1,700 t of metal meant for Zaporizhzhia fortifications, and sentenced to five years.
notes: count_generic used for mass of metal; unit t.

text: Russia retook Robotyne in 2024, according to secondary sources.
By August 2026 Russian groups took eastern Mala Tokmachka.

The Robotyne diorama is a box of about 25 × 20 km, running from Kopani and Nesterianka in the west to Verbove and Novofedorivka in the east, and from Orikhiv in the north to Novoprokopivka and Ocheretuvate in the south, with Tokmak just off the southern edge.
Orikhiv lies at 47.5754, 35.7855 (OSM), elevation ~53 m (SRTM), 15.0 km N of Robotyne.

Lobkove lies at 47.5229, 35.4409 and Piatykhatky at 47.5083, 35.4615 (OSM), 30.3 km and 28.3 km west of Robotyne.

text: Lobkove and Piatykhatky formed the western sub-axis of the Ukrainian offensive in June 2023.

The ground on the Orikhiv axis climbs from the Kinska valley at Orikhiv (about 51–53 m) and Mala Tokmachka (about 68 m) to about 120–140 m on the Robotyne–Kopani ridge, peaking at about 152 m just south of Robotyne.
The Ukrainian attackers on the Orikhiv axis advanced up a long, open slope under observation.
The Zaporizhzhia steppe is flat to gently rolling, which makes for long sight lines.

In the OSM and Sentinel-2 sample box around Robotyne, tree lines run roughly E–W and N–S; main belts are about 0.5–0.6 km apart and cross-belts about 1.0–1.2 km apart, at 1.34 km of mapped belt per km².

observations.value_text: 1.34 km of mapped belt per km²

text: Kofman and Lee described the 2023 southern fighting as "a war of tree lines, with shifts in the line often counted in hundreds of meters".
Ravines (balkas) separate the "platforms" of high ground, as described at Rivnopil on the neighbouring axis.
The Balka Uspenivka southeast of Orikhiv was a named fighting area in August 2023.
A Ukrainian mine-action officer reported in June 2023 that Russia was regularly blowing up small dams in the south to disrupt Ukrainian operations.
Col. Petro Chernyk described the Russian defence in three echelons: minefields "several kilometers deep", then a line with artillery and troops, then rear positions.
RUSI puts the Russian Orikhiv–Tokmak defence at about 30 km deep in three lines.
Robotyne marked the southern edge of the densest Russian minefields on the Orikhiv axis.
Beyond Robotyne lay "a relatively more contiguous array" of anti-tank ditch, dragon's teeth and minefields with fighting positions behind them.
West of Verbove the next Russian belt runs about 1.7–3.5 km from the village.

observations.subject: distance of the belt west of Verbove from the village

text: Ukrainian assault troops described the Surovikin-line trenches as "usually 2-3 meters deep, reinforced with wood and earth".
Russian anti-tank ditches on the Surovikin line were 4 m deep and 6 m wide.
Russian minefields grew from 120 m to about 500 m deep, with mines stacked two high.
Russian barrier minefields ran "sometimes as much as 5 or more kilometers deep".
The T0408 (Т-04-08) runs north–south from Orikhiv through Novodanylivka, Robotyne and Novoprokopivka to Tokmak, and is the axis of the whole Robotyne chapter.
Shtupun noted in August 2023 that Robotyne sits on "the highway to Tokmak".
By 4 October 2023 Ukraine held a trench along the T0408 between Robotyne and Novoprokopivka.
The N08 (Н-08) shares the T0408 out of Orikhiv to Novodanylivka, then runs east past Novopokrovka (about 2 km) and Novofedorivka (about 1.3 km), about 6 km north of Verbove, towards Polohy.
The N08 is the "Polohy–Voskresenka highway" that Ukrainian forces crossed on 8 June 2023 and later claimed near Verbove in September 2023.
The T0815 (Т-08-15) runs through Mala Tokmachka towards Novopokrovka.
Mapped tracks are sparse around Robotyne, at 0.34 km per km² in the sample box, and movement was along field edges and tree lines.
On 7–10 June 2023 the Orikhiv axis (ERA5, 47.47 N 35.85 E) was dry and warm, with highs of 24–27 °C, lows of 9–17 °C and no rain.
Cloud over the Orikhiv axis rose from 69% on 7 June 2023 to 79% on 8 June and 100% on 10 June.
On the Orikhiv axis in early June 2023 sunrise was at 04:40 and sunset at 20:30 local time.
Rain followed on 11–12 June 2023 on the Orikhiv axis, 27 mm.
In June 2023 night lasted only about eight hours, so an assault that slipped two hours, as one did in the opening assaults, ran into dawn.
Russian sources reported Ukrainian attacks rising "due to improved weather" by 15 June 2023.
July–August 2023 on the Orikhiv axis was hot and dry: August means were 30 °C high and 19 °C low, with a peak of 36.8 °C and only 32 mm of rain.
On the Orikhiv axis the high was 30 °C on 26 July 2023, 27 °C on 23 August and 33 °C on 28 August.
Ukrainian soldiers fought without body armour in the heat in summer 2023.
September 2023 on the Orikhiv axis was dry and clear: 24 mm of rain, highs of 25–27 °C on 20–23 September, and sunset falling to about 18:35.
November 2023 on the Orikhiv axis brought 101 mm of rain on 19 days and a storm on 26–27 November, with gusts to about 46 km/h, then a low of −1.9 °C.
Milbloggers said at the end of November 2023 that the weather on the Orikhiv axis impeded vehicles and artillery but not drones.
Gen. Valerii Zaluzhnyi was Ukraine's commander-in-chief during the 2023 counteroffensive.
Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi commanded the Tavria group, which commanded the southern front in 2023.
The Tavria group's spokesmen in 2023 were Valerii Shershen, then Oleksandr Shtupun.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade was commanded by Lt. Col. Oleksandr Sak until 16 September 2023, then by Col. Oleksandr Pavlii.
RUSI says the plan was for 12 armoured and mechanised brigades on a 30 km front to isolate Tokmak in seven days.
RUSI says that in the event only a couple of Ukrainian brigades were properly equipped for the 2023 offensive.
The US wanted one massed southern axis for the 2023 counteroffensive, but Ukraine split its effort across three axes: Orikhiv, Velyka Novosilka and Bakhmut.
A secondary NYT account (2025), relayed by Wikipedia, says Zelensky split the 12 new brigades seven to Tarnavskyi and five to Syrskyi; this was not verified in the dossier.
In the first echelon on the Orikhiv axis in 2023 was the 9th Corps.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade "Magura" was built from scratch around Markus's volunteer "brand", and its troops trained in NATO countries.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade was equipped with M2A2 ODS Bradleys and Leopard 2s.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade had Soviet T-64s fitted with mine rollers.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade had an engineer element with Leopard 2R and Wisent breaching tanks and a BMR-2.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade's casualties are reported at about 2,000 of 5,000 by September 2023 (El País via Wikipedia, not verified in the dossier).
notes: Unverified; rests on El País via Wikipedia.

text: The 33rd Mechanised Brigade supplied the Leopard 2A6s seen on 8 June 2023.
The 65th Mechanised Brigade supported on the Orikhiv axis and was photographed near Robotyne on 1 October 2023.
Supporting units on the Orikhiv axis included the 128th Mountain Assault Brigade and the 15th National Guard Brigade.

The second echelon on the Orikhiv axis, the 10th Corps, was committed at the end of July 2023: the NATO-trained 116th, 117th and 118th Mechanised Brigades and the 3rd and 14th National Guard Brigades.
The Ukrainian reserves on the Orikhiv axis, the 46th Airmobile Brigade and the 82nd Air Assault Brigade, were committed in mid-August 2023.
Per the leaked US documents, the 82nd Air Assault Brigade had 40 Marders, 90 Strykers and 14 Challenger 2s.
The 82nd Air Assault Brigade's crews came from the 25th and 80th Brigades and were trained in the UK.
Elements of the 73rd Naval Special Operations Centre fought at Robotyne.
At most about 55 Ukrainian 155 mm guns fired on the main axis, at about 70 rounds a gun a day at peak and as few as 10.

observations.subject: 155 mm guns on the main axis

text: About 7 GMLRS a day were available to Ukraine for the whole theatre in 2023.
Ukraine used Storm Shadow and SCALP against Russian headquarters in 2023.
US cluster munitions (DPICM) arrived in Ukraine in July 2023.
On 10 September 2023 Tarnavskyi claimed 1,391 artillery engagements in one day.
Ukrainian breaching kit was scarce in 2023, and the M1150 Assault Breacher was usable only from October.
About 109 M2A2 ODS Bradleys and 21 Leopard 2A6s had been delivered to Ukraine by June 2023.
All six Finnish Leopard 2Rs went to Ukraine.
Abrams tanks arrived in Ukraine only on 23 September 2023, too late for the counteroffensive.
In "an hour or two" of fighting on 8 June 2023 Ukraine lost about a fifth of its Bradleys and Leopard 2A6s and half its Leopard 2Rs (Forbes, via Censor.NET).
Many Ukrainian vehicles lost in June 2023 were immobilised rather than destroyed and were later recovered and repaired.
A 47th Mechanised Brigade assault commander claimed "every last vehicle was successfully retrieved" from the row of eight disabled Bradleys and a Leopard.
By 6 September 2023 five Leopard 2s (Forbes) and one Challenger 2 had been destroyed in the counteroffensive.
By mid-December 2023 the 47th Mechanised Brigade had lost about 30 Bradleys and had about a dozen Leopard 2A6s left.
Oryx whole-war Ukrainian loss totals to October 2026 are 13 Leopard 2A6, 4 Leopard 2R, 3 Challenger 2, 189 M2A2 ODS-SA Bradleys and 12 Wisent 1.
notes: Whole-war totals, not the chapter window. Whole-war cumulative totals; no single era.

text: Col. Gen. Alexander Romanchuk commanded the Russian Zaporizhzhia grouping in 2023.
Romanchuk was wounded on 22 September 2023, by Budanov's account.
The 58th Combined Arms Army was commanded by Maj. Gen. Ivan Popov until about 11–12 July 2023, then by Lt. Gen. Denis Lyamin, who was reportedly removed on 9 October 2023.

Above the Zaporizhzhia grouping were Gerasimov, who was claimed to have taken over the south on 5 June 2023, the VDV's Teplinsky and the Southern Military District's Kuzovlev; the chain of command was unclear.
The 58th Combined Arms Army's headquarters was in Berdiansk in 2023.
The 42nd Guards Motor Rifle Division (58th Army) fielded the 70th and 291st Regiments, which held the line on 7–8 June 2023, and the 71st at Robotyne.
The Russian 19th Motor Rifle Division fielded the 429th Regiment southwest of Orikhiv and the 503rd, moved from Nesterianka to Robotyne in August 2023.
The GRU Spetsnaz 22nd and 45th Brigades were the counterattack force behind the Russian first line on the Orikhiv axis.
The Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade fought at Robotyne in 2023.
Budanov called the 810th Naval Infantry Brigade "completely defeated" in September 2023 (Wikipedia summary of ISW).
The Russian 1429th and 1430th territorial-troops regiments fought at Robotyne in 2023.
Russian volunteer units at Robotyne in 2023 included BARS, "Storm Ossetia" and "Alania", Vostok-Akhmat and Yug-Akhmat, and "Osman".
The Russian 7th Guards VDV Division (56th, 108th and 247th Regiments) was transferred laterally from Kherson to the Orikhiv axis from about mid-August 2023.
The Russian 76th Guards VDV Division was transferred from Kreminna to the Orikhiv axis in late August 2023.
The Russian 41st Combined Arms Army was transferred to the Orikhiv axis from about 1 September 2023.
The UK MoD counted at least five VDV regiments near Robotyne, "dramatically under strength".
Kivliuk named the re-formed Russian 44th and 104th airborne divisions on the southern front.
The Russian 136th Motor Rifle Brigade took over 42nd Division sectors in November 2023.
RUSI says Russia had up to 105,000 troops on the Orikhiv axis, about 470 tanks, up to 1,410 AFVs, 720+ guns, up to 230 MLRS and 12 operational-tactical missile complexes.
RUSI says each 10 km of the Russian front on the Orikhiv axis was held by a motor-rifle regiment plus an airborne regiment.

observations.subject: front per motor-rifle regiment plus airborne regiment

text: RUSI says the Russian guns on the Orikhiv axis had 35 days of ammunition, and there were about 60 attack helicopters.
Forbes, via Wikipedia, put "perhaps 10,000 or more" Russian troops in the 42nd Division's regiments near Tokmak on 8 June 2023.
There were 27 Russian helicopters at Berdiansk by 13 June 2023, including 5 Ka-52.

WarSpotting has about 156 visually confirmed Russian equipment losses tagged to the Orikhiv axis for 1 June – 30 November 2023: 41 tanks, 62 IFVs and APCs and a Ka-52M on 17 August, with 82 of them by the end of August.
Among the most common Russian equipment losses on the Orikhiv axis in June–November 2023 were the BTR-82A, MT-LB, T-80BV, T-72B3 and BMD-4M.
Shtupun said on 27 August 2023 that Russia was "irrevocably losing up to 100 people daily".
Popov himself complained of "mass deaths and injuries" from Ukrainian artillery.
ISW judged the Russian response on 8 June 2023 "doctrinally sound": the first echelon slowed the attack with mines and strongpoints, fell back to a second line, and reserves retook the first line.
By Tarnavskyi's count Russia put 60% of its defensive effort into the first belt on the southern front.

observations.subject: Russian effort in the first belt

text: Kofman contrasts Surovikin's positional defence with Gerasimov's "active defence" of constant flank counterattacks.
Russian minefields on the southern front were deepened to about 500 m, with stacked anti-tank mines and mixed anti-tank and anti-personnel fields.
The Russian ISDM Zemledeliye system scattered mines remotely.
Russian artillery-delivered mines made Ukrainian night resupply through the minefield lanes deadly.
Russia left remote-detonated mines in empty trenches.
Russia re-mined cleared ground on the Orikhiv axis in October 2023.
A 47th Mechanised Brigade T-64 commander said mine rollers normally survive "up to four explosions", but stacked mines destroyed one after a single blast.

observations.subject: explosions a mine roller normally survives

text: In the Russian kill chain on the southern front, drones spot a column, and artillery, ATGMs, Ka-52s, Lancets and FPVs follow.
Kofman and Lee: "In many cases, a tank or armored vehicle will become immobilized after hitting a mine and then be destroyed by attack helicopters or drones."

cites.quote: In many cases, a tank or armored vehicle will become immobilized after hitting a mine and then be destroyed by attack helicopters or drones

text: Russia moved to Krasnopol and Lancet strikes on Ukrainian lead elements, "effect over volume".
Russian EW disrupted Ukrainian GPS, radios and drones on the southern front in June 2023.
Russian guided glide bombs pounded Orikhiv and Verbove in 2023.
The UK MoD called the Ka-52 "one of the most influential Russian weapons systems" against the 2023 offensive.
The Ka-52 struck with Vikhr missiles from 8–10 km, often with an EW escort.
Ka-52 strikes were heralded by the lifting of Russian GPS jamming.
The Ka-52M carried LMUR missiles to about 15 km, beyond Ukrainian tactical air defence.
Lofted S-8 rockets gave Russian attack helicopters a further 6–7 km of reach.
On 8 June 2023 the Ukrainian column south of Mala Tokmachka foundered under Ka-52 Vikhr fire.
MANPADS from the 47th Mechanised Brigade countered the Ka-52, downing the brigade's eighth Ka-52 on 17 August 2023.

observations.subject: Ka-52s downed by the 47th Mechanised Brigade (cumulative)

text: Ukraine struck the Berdiansk helicopter base with ATACMS on 17 October 2023.
Russian sources say Ka-52 use fell after the mid-August 2023 losses.
Russian Lancets hunted Ukrainian guns and lead vehicles on the southern front.
A Lancet-3 targeted an abandoned Leopard 2A6 after 8 June 2023, with ambiguous results.
A Lancet hit a Stryker of the 82nd Air Assault Brigade east of Robotyne on 15 August 2023.
The Ukrainian June 2023 breach was designed as a company-size combined-arms breach behind mine-clearing vehicles, using the Leopard 2R, Wisent, BMR-2, M58 MICLIC, UR-77 and Meteorit line charges.
In the June 2023 breach the Ukrainian lanes were too shallow, and crews strayed off them.
In the June 2023 breach Ukrainian columns stacked up on single lanes.
In the June 2023 breach one Ukrainian unit was late, another fired on friendly troops, and another was disoriented at night.
Ukraine fired only 3% of its fire missions as smoke, because smoke blinded its own drone feeds.
A Ukrainian Leopard crew had trained on minefields of "100 by 200 meters" and faced "hectares".
A Ukrainian soldier said the Americans taught Stinger drills from rooftops that would not survive the first tank shells.
From July 2023 Ukrainian dismounted assault groups, platoons and companies of 10–15-man squads, moved along tree lines, mostly on foot.
The Ukrainian dismounted advance went at 700–1,200 m every five days.
Each Ukrainian battalion yielded only about two platoons of assault-capable troops.
Ukrainian engineers cleared mines by hand at night.
Bradleys served as "taxis" that delivered and recovered Ukrainian assault groups, and survived mines and a near-direct 120 mm mortar hit.
In tank raids, Leopard 2A6s fired HE into tree lines and pulled back at the first Russian round.
Ukrainian tanks ran along tree lines to set off anti-personnel mines for the infantry.
The Ukrainian counter-battery war on the southern front used GMLRS and FPVs.
The Ukrainian counter-battery war used radar-hunting.
The Ukrainian counter-battery war used night bombing with converted agricultural drones.
Popov's complaint about counter-battery fire is the Russian side of the Ukrainian counter-battery war.
Ukrainian Storm Shadow strikes hit Russian headquarters and generals.
Russian FPVs took the edge at small-unit level by September 2023; a 47th Mechanised Brigade sergeant said: "Our enemy has learned and adapted".
Ukraine lacked air cover against Russian glide bombs and helicopters in 2023.
In the breach south of Mala Tokmachka on 7–9 June 2023, twenty Ukrainian vehicles in two groups moved up a wide muddy track between hedgerows behind a Leopard 2R and a BMR-2.

South of Mala Tokmachka in June 2023 the first Ukrainian group hit mines and gave itself away; drones then found the second, and shells and Ka-52 missiles fell on vehicles bunched "too close together near a minefield".

Inside the kill zone south of Mala Tokmachka, Ukrainian infantry ran through the smoke between vehicles, and a Bradley crew popped smoke and covered the dismounts as they climbed onto it, wary of mines beside the track.
Four more Bradleys drove into the kill zone south of Mala Tokmachka to retrieve Ukrainian troops.
The drone image of a Leopard 2A6 and eight Bradleys in a row south of Mala Tokmachka became the offensive's emblem.
The Russian MoD later paraded a Leopard captured south of Mala Tokmachka.
Markus says five Ukrainian soldiers were lost in the breach south of Mala Tokmachka.
Most Ukrainian crews south of Mala Tokmachka escaped through open hatches and lowered ramps.

Before dawn on 8 June 2023 a Ukrainian assault group slipped between two Russian companies and took a tactical height by 05:00, then shelled the next height for three hours; a soldier could see Polohy through binoculars.
In his 12 July 2023 voice memo, the fired 58th Army commander Popov ("Spartacus") addressed his "gladiators": "we were hit from behind by our highest boss, treacherously and vilely".
Popov's voice memo came a day after a Storm Shadow strike on his reserve command post.

mentions.name: Storm Shadow strike on the 58th Army reserve command post

text: On 26 July 2023 company-size Ukrainian mechanized groups broke into the first Russian positions east of Robotyne, until Bradleys and a T-72 were left 2.5 km due east of the village; a lone vehicle reached the anti-tank positions near Verbove.

observations.subject: abandoned vehicles due east of Robotyne

text: On 22–23 August 2023 a 47th Mechanised Brigade assault group briefed to take positions outside Robotyne was told mid-move to take the first houses, then told again that friendly troops were further in: "In the space of a day, we moved forward more than two kilometers".
The 47th Mechanised Brigade filmed civilians being led out of Robotyne with journalists present, and raised the flag on 23 August 2023.
On 17 August 2023 a single MANPADS launch by the 47th Mechanised Brigade downed a Ka-52 near Robotyne, the brigade's eighth.

observations.subject: Ka-52s downed by the 47th Mechanised Brigade (cumulative)

text: WarSpotting logs a Ka-52M lost near Novoprokopivka on 17 August 2023.
On 20–23 September 2023 Ukrainian armoured vehicles crossed the anti-tank ditch and dragon's teeth west of Verbove, and an MRAP and a BMP-2 burned beyond the trench line.
Tarnavskyi announced a "breakthrough" on the left flank at Verbove in September 2023.
On 5 September 2023 a Challenger 2 near Robotyne was hit by artillery, its crew fought the fire, it was hit again, and all the crew survived.
In spring 2023 US planners urged a massed mechanized assault on the southern axis alone.
Ukraine decided in spring 2023 to split its forces across three axes to stretch Russia, rather than mass on the southern axis as US planners urged.
Kofman and Lee read Ukraine's split across three axes as probing for the weakest point.
US officials later blamed the dispersal of Ukrainian forces and continued investment around Bakhmut for the counteroffensive's results.
Ukrainians replied that the US misunderstood the drone-saturated battlefield and withheld air power.
RUSI says Ukraine went into the 2023 offensive with only a couple of properly equipped brigades.
The Pentagon wanted a mid-April 2023 start; Kyiv waited for equipment and training, and the attack began in June.
Zelensky said the delay of the 2023 offensive gave Russia time to fortify (relayed by Wikipedia).
RUSI adds that poor Ukrainian operational security meant Russia knew the axis and timing of the 2023 offensive.
The untested 47th Mechanised Brigade was given a frontal attack where the Russian lines were most concentrated.
Western officials and analysts argued that any force would have struggled to breach the Russian lines without air superiority or enough breaching kit.
On "the fourth day" of the offensive, about 11–12 June 2023, Zaluzhnyi halted frontal assaults to save Western vehicles and switched to infantry-led attrition (WaPo, via Euromaidan Press).
Kofman and Lee describe the same switch from mechanized assault to infantry-led attrition in June 2023.
The trade-off of halting the armour was fewer armour losses, a slower advance and more time for the defender to reset.
The Ukrainian 10th Corps was meant to pass through a breach that the 9th Corps had not made when it was committed in late July 2023.
The New York Times reported much of the Ukrainian reserve committed on 26 July 2023.
The 82nd and 46th Brigades then gave quicker results, "enabled by other units having spent weeks of fighting over those areas".
RUSI judged a Ukrainian breakthrough likeliest in early August 2023.
In July 2023 Popov raised counter-battery and rotation problems "at the highest level" and was fired by order of the defence minister.
ISW read Popov's appeal as an attempt to go over Gerasimov to Putin; it judged Russia had no reserves to grant rotation, and the effect of his dismissal on the defence marginal.
Rather than rotating exhausted units in August–September 2023, Moscow moved in the 7th and 76th VDV Divisions and the 41st Combined Arms Army, accepting risk at Kherson and Kreminna.
These were the third Russian lateral transfer of the counteroffensive and the second in a few weeks.
In September 2023 Tarnavskyi set Tokmak as "the minimum goal" and promised to fight through winter on foot.
A secondary NYT account (2025), relayed by Wikipedia, says the aim of the offensive had already shrunk from Melitopol to Tokmak.

A secondary NYT account (2025), relayed by Wikipedia, says US suggestions to replace Tarnavskyi or send the marines to Robotyne were overruled, and Zaluzhnyi sent the marines across the Dnipro instead.
notes: Not verified in the dossier; see the Krynky chapter.

text: Zaluzhnyi's "stalemate" essay in The Economist in November 2023 signalled that the offensive was over.
Zaluzhnyi's "stalemate" essay in November 2023 opened a rift with Zelensky.
In June 2023 the Russian MoD praised the Southern Military District with "an uncharacteristic degree of coherency".
Romanchuk said the Ukrainian attack in June 2023 was telegraphed by artillery preparation.
Popov credited the 58th Army's minefields with the June 2023 defence.
The Russian MoD claimed 150 Ukrainian tanks and AFVs were used in June 2023 and 30 tanks destroyed, including 3 Leopards.

observations.subject: Ukrainian tanks and AFVs used (Russian MoD claim)

notes: ISW called Russian destroyed-vehicle claims highly inflated.

text: Unofficial Russian sources stressed that Ukraine was using far more wheeled vehicles than tanks in June 2023.
ISW called the Russian claims of destroyed Ukrainian vehicles in June 2023 "highly inflated".
DeepState said Russia recirculated the same footage of the June 2023 breach from new angles.
Russian milbloggers explained the June 2023 defence by EW, an "unprecedented" amount of helicopter support, landmines and layered fortifications.
Russian milbloggers described a "strategic defense" to attrit Ukraine on the first line in June 2023.
Some Russian milbloggers prematurely declared the Ukrainian counteroffensive failed in June 2023.
Popov said: "The armed forces of Ukraine couldn't break through our army on the frontline; we were hit from behind by our highest boss".
Russian milbloggers called Popov "intelligent" and "competent", and none disputed his complaints.
In 2025 Popov was jailed for stealing metal meant for the very fortifications his army defended.
In August 2023 Russian milbloggers wrote of exhausted, unrotated units on the Zaporizhzhia front.
In August 2023 Russian milbloggers called the situation at Verbove "very dangerous".
In August 2023 Russian milbloggers worried about the Robotyne–Verbove line.
Shoigu called Zaporizhzhia "the tensest" direction in September 2023.
In September 2023 a Kremlin-affiliated milblogger insisted the "Surovikin" line west of Verbove was unbroken.
"Storm Ossetia" and "Alania" called reports of a Ukrainian breakthrough false in September 2023.
Russian sources later credited the Ka-52 with disrupting the early Ukrainian assaults.
Shoigu claimed over 90,000 Ukrainian killed and wounded, almost 600 tanks and about 1,900 armoured vehicles across the counteroffensive; ISW called this "implausible".
RUSI calls the Russian 2023 defence "textbook": three belts, rotated regiments, cached ammunition, Lancets and helicopters, and early glide bombs.
Kofman and Lee note that, unlike in Kherson in 2022, Russia manned its forward positions most heavily in 2023.
The coordinates of key locations in the Robotyne diorama are OSM place nodes.
The elevations of key locations in the Robotyne diorama are SRTM 30 m values, and distances are great-circle from Robotyne.

counter: deep layered minefields with stacked anti-tank mines
measure: mechanized breach of the Surovikin line (Leopard 2R, Wisent, BMR-2, MICLIC, UR-77)
rationale: Mines, deepened from 120 m to about 500 m and stacked, immobilised the 47th Mechanised Brigade's columns south of Mala Tokmachka on 7–8 June 2023; the breach lanes were too shallow and crews strayed off them.
effect: stopped the June 2023 breach; Western armour assaults halted within days

counter: Ka-52 stand-off fire (Vikhr from 8–10 km, LMUR to about 15 km, lofted S-8)
measure: mechanized breach columns stalled in minefields
rationale: Columns bunched near minefields were hit by Ka-52 missiles; the Vikhr outranged Ukrainian tactical air defence and the LMUR reached about 15 km.
effect: vehicles immobilised by mines were destroyed or the column foundered

counter: drone-cued kill chain (drones spot, then artillery, ATGMs, Ka-52s, Lancets and FPVs strike)
rationale: Drones found the second Ukrainian group on 7 June and artillery followed; Kofman and Lee describe immobilised vehicles finished by helicopters or drones.

counter: dismounted small-unit assault groups moving along tree lines
measure: deep Russian minefields and the anti-armour kill chain
rationale: After Zaluzhnyi halted the armour about 11–12 June 2023, platoons of 10–15-man squads advanced mostly on foot along tree lines, trading speed for fewer vehicle losses, and took Robotyne in August.
effect: fewer armour losses but an advance of only 700–1,200 m every five days

counter: night hand demining by engineers
measure: Russian minefields in front of the first belt
rationale: Ukrainian engineers cleared mines by hand at night, the only time Tarnavskyi said clearing was possible.

counter: Russian re-mining of cleared ground (including remote mining by ISDM Zemledeliye)
rationale: Russia re-mined the cleared Robotyne–Verbove area in October 2023 and could scatter mines remotely with the Zemledeliye system.

counter: stacked anti-tank mines
rationale: A 47th Brigade T-64 commander said rollers normally survive up to four explosions, but stacked mines destroyed one after a single blast.
effect: mine roller destroyed after a single blast

counter: artillery-delivered mines
measure: Ukrainian night resupply through minefield lanes
rationale: RUSI says artillery-delivered mines made night resupply through the lanes deadly.

counter: MANPADS
rationale: The 47th Brigade's MANPADS downed its eighth Ka-52 near Robotyne on 17 August 2023, and Russian sources say Ka-52 use fell after the mid-August losses.
effect: Ka-52 losses mounted and their use fell after mid-August

counter: ATACMS strike on the Berdiansk helicopter base
rationale: Ukraine's first ATACMS strike on 17 October 2023 hit the Berdiansk helicopter base, where 27 helicopters including 5 Ka-52 had gathered by 13 June.

counter: Ukrainian counter-battery fire (GMLRS, FPVs, radar-hunting, night drone bombing)
rationale: Ukraine's counter-battery war used GMLRS, FPVs, radar-hunting and converted agricultural drones; Popov complained of counter-battery and artillery-reconnaissance problems and was fired.
effect: degraded Russian artillery; Russian counter-battery problems worst in the Zaporizhzhia direction

counter: Storm Shadow deep strikes
rationale: Storm Shadow hit headquarters and generals, including the 58th Army's reserve command post near Berdiansk on 11 July 2023, reportedly killing Lt. Gen. Tsokov.

counter: Russian FPV drones
rationale: By September 2023 Russian FPVs took the edge at small-unit level; a 47th Brigade sergeant said the enemy had learned and adapted.
effect: took the edge at small-unit level

counter: Lancet and Krasnopol precision strikes on lead elements
rationale: Russia moved to Krasnopol and Lancet strikes on lead elements, effect over volume; a Lancet hit an 82nd Brigade Stryker east of Robotyne on 15 August 2023.

counter: Bradley used as an armoured "taxi"
measure: mines and mortar fire on assault-group delivery and recovery
rationale: Bradleys delivered and recovered Ukrainian assault groups and survived mines and a near-direct 120 mm mortar hit.
effect: survived mines and a near-direct 120 mm mortar hit

counter: tanks running along tree lines
rationale: Ukrainian tanks ran along tree lines to set off anti-personnel mines for the infantry.
effect: set off anti-personnel mines ahead of the infantry

counter: Russian lateral transfers of VDV divisions and the 41st Combined Arms Army
measure: Ukrainian penetration at Robotyne and Verbove
rationale: Rather than rotating units, Moscow moved in the 7th and 76th VDV and the 41st Army, and the salient stopped short of Novoprokopivka and Verbove.
effect: no breakthrough to Tokmak; front positional by November

counter: Russian first-echelon defence with counterattacking reserves
rationale: On 8 June 2023 the first echelon slowed the attack with mines and strongpoints and fell back, and reserves retook the first line; a first-line position of the 291st and 70th Regiments was penetrated, then retaken.

counter: Russian EW and GPS jamming
rationale: Russian EW disrupted Ukrainian GPS, radios and drones in June 2023, and its lifting heralded Ka-52 strikes.

counter: Russian surveillance drones
rationale: Ukraine fired only 3% of its fire missions as smoke because smoke blinded its own drone feeds, leaving its columns exposed to Russian observation.
effect: smoke used sparingly (3% of fire missions)
